## Checklist

- [ ] The tool is open-source or free-to-use with clearly documented terms
- [ ] The repository has had at least one commit in the last 18 months (or is historically significant)
- [ ] The tool is relevant to professional hardware design engineers
- [ ] It is not already listed in the README (I searched with Ctrl+F)
- [ ] The tool has working documentation that a new user can follow
